title: Done means verified
lesson: An agent's "done" is a claim; the harness runs the end-to-end check and flips a feature to passing only on its own evidence, so a failed claim goes back to the agent while the record stays false.
limitations: Audio verified analytically (peak -6.6 dBFS, spectrogram, onset alignment of 55 of 61 cues; the six quiet ack and first clock ticks were merged by the detector); no physical listening.
Frame legibility checked from decoded frames at full size and 350 px, not on a real phone.
Illustrative scenario: two features, one failing run, no measured timings or pass rates.
Shows the harness owning the test run and the record write; the source article has the agent self-verify under prompted rules, which prompts alone do not enforce.

transcript.text: The agent works on feature A, then sends the harness a DONE claim. The feature list row for A turns orange: claimed but not yet verified.
The harness runs the end-to-end tests for A. They pass, and only then does the harness write "A passes:true" to the feature list, which turns green.
The agent works on feature B and sends the same DONE claim. The harness runs the tests for B and they fail.
The feature list row for B stays "passes:false"; the harness returns the failed claim to the agent, which jolts red. The claim alone changed nothing.
The agent fixes B and claims DONE again. The harness re-runs the tests, they pass, and "B passes:true" is written with a chime: every feature is now verified.
The list holds both features green, then the frame fades to black.
